cases.input: A famous physicist says a specific tax policy will definitely increase employment, therefore the forecast is correct.
best_questions: Is the source expert in the economic/labor domain relevant to the forecast?
What evidence or model supports the employment prediction?

cases.input: After a school introduced a new app, grades rose, so the app caused the improvement.
Running a city is like running a household, so a city should never borrow money.
Policy P will probably increase average output, therefore P is the right policy.
No one has proven that the new process is unsafe, therefore it is proven safe.

Claim: a medication policy reduced errors because errors fell after adoption. Candidate questions include: (A) What color is the policy document? (B) Did measurement/reporting rules change at the same time? (C) Do staff like the policy? (D) What other interventions occurred concurrently?
Speaker says: 'This rule usually helps because it reduces queue time.' A critic strengthens it to 'This rule always helps everyone' and then defeats that stronger version with one exception.
An argument cites an expert who also presents a causal study. The conclusion relies both on the source's expertise and on the study design.
